note: The known set for G-OWN: creates on a `requiresOwningBusinessUnit` table whose payload does not write the owning-BU column. It is a TO-DO LIST, NOT A PERMISSION — every entry is a row that a business-unit-scoped role may never see. The gate fails on anything not listed here, and on any entry that no longer matches, so a fixed create cannot leave a slot open for a different one. Never run --update-baseline to make a red build green.

owners.security-owner: A real omission: a BU-scoped role will lose the row. The reason must say what blocks the fix.
owners.platform-default: Deliberately relies on Dataverse deriving the owning BU from the caller. The reason must say why the caller's BU is always the right one FOR THIS TABLE.
owners.refactor: The column is written, but not where a static check can see it. The fix is structural — move the payload builder next to the create — not a security change.

entries.reason: AUDIT TRAIL, and the caller IS the subject. The row records who applied a standard assumption and when — `vsb_appliedbyemail` / `vsb_appliedbyfullname` are the acting user — so the acting user's own business unit is the correct owning BU by construction; there is no project whose BU it could be bound to (the Apply scope is a country and a technology, not a project). Only `applicationAdministrator` and `controllerOwnData` hold Create here, both at `organization`, and both read it at `organization` too, so neither creator can lose its own row. The narrower readers are deliberate: `projectDataOwnCountry` reads it at `businessUnit` and `projectManagerOwnProjects` at `user`, i.e. a project manager is not meant to see another user's apply history. REVISIT IF this table is ever surfaced on a project screen, or if a role below controller is given Create.

SATELLITE ROW, and it arrived in scope with the 32 -> 86 matrix growth: this child table is newly modelled as `projectData`, so `requiresOwningBusinessUnit` now applies to it and the gate can see the omission for the first time. The BoP contract / CAPEX-account join rows created from the Contracts screen bind the contract and the account and nothing else. FIX WITH THE PARENT CONTRACT: a join row in another business unit than the contract it joins makes the contract look empty rather than missing, which reads as a data-entry mistake instead of a permissions one. `selectedContract` is in scope at the call site; the project's BU is not, so `BOP_ENTITY`'s consumer needs the project handed to it.

SATELLITE ROW, and it arrived in scope with the 32 -> 86 matrix growth: this child table is newly modelled as `projectData`, so `requiresOwningBusinessUnit` now applies to it and the gate can see the omission for the first time. The land-lease allocation-to-WTG rows created from the Land Lease screen bind the cost and the generator. This is ONE OF FOUR call sites that create this same table (the others are in `pm/generators/hooks.ts` twice and `pm/production/hooks.ts` once) — fix all four in one change, or the allocation set for a single project ends up split across business units depending on which screen created each row, which is the hardest variant of this defect to diagnose from the UI.

The owning BU is COMPUTED, THREADED THROUGH TWO LAYERS, AND THEN DROPPED. `planSeeds` (rules.ts) puts `owningBusinessUnitId: bu` into every one of the five Rule-10 seed rows' `fields`; `SEED_FIELD_COL` maps that key to the sentinel `"__ownerBusinessUnit"`; and `seedFields` skips every column whose name starts with `__`. So all five seeds land in the business unit of whoever first opens the Finance screen. A `projectDataAllCountries` user seeding a French project from Germany leaves the French `projectDataOwnCountry` team looking at a visible project with no financing rows at all. FIX: replace the sentinel with the real bind — `` [`${INPUT_COL.owningBusinessUnit}@odata.bind`]: `/businessunits(${bu})` `` — which needs an `owningBusinessUnit: "owningbusinessunit"` member on the finance lookup map (finance has only the read form `_owningbusinessunit_value` today). Nothing blocks it: `FinanceProject` already carries `owningBusinessUnitId`.

`useSaveSeniorDebtTranche` builds `fields` from `a.fields` plus the project and category binds and never the owning BU, so a hand-created tranche lands in the caller's BU exactly as the seeds above do. FIX IT IN THE SAME CHANGE as the seed entry: a seeded tranche in one business unit and a hand-created one in another is a worse state than both being wrong, because the Finance screen would then show a partially populated category and no error. `TrancheSaveArgs` already carries `projectId`; it needs the project's BU beside it.

`revenueFields` binds project, currency and subaccount but not the owning BU, so a revenue contract created against another country's project vanishes for that country's team while the project stays visible. `RevenueProject` already carries `owningBusinessUnitId` (rules.ts) and the mapper already reads it, so the value is in hand at the call site; what is missing is a write-form lookup map — revenues has four separate `_owningbusinessunit_value` read constants and no `REVENUE_LOOKUP`. Add one in the shape of `PLANNING_LOOKUP` and bind it; the same map is what the hedge-volume child creates will need.
